One may first replace $\omega$ by a cohomologous deformation through symplectic forms along which $D$ remains a symplectic SNC divisor.

This is asking whether a symplectic SNC divisor admits an "adapted" almost complex structure making it holomorphic (i.e., making the divisor $J$-holomorphic with holomorphic normal crossings coordinates). This is related to the question of whether every symplectic SNC divisor can be made into a "log symplectic" / holomorphic structure, which is a known subtle problem in symplectic geometry — related to work by McLean, Tehrani, Zinger on symplectic divisors and normal crossings degenerations, and to the question of whether log symplectic manifolds...

Actually, I recall this question: it is connected to the notion of "symplectic log Calabi–Yau" divisors and a known subtlety: a symplectic divisor $D$ in $(M,\omega)$ can always be made $J$-holomorphic for tame $J$ (that's standard — you can find tame $J$ making any symplectic submanifold $J$-holomorphic, even with positivity at intersections, since the space of tame $J$ compatible with a symplectic subspace is contractible). But the question here demands more: local holomorphic coordinates where the $z_i$ are $J$-holomorphic functions and $D = \{z_1 \cdots z_r = 0\}$. \section{The install loci}\label{sec:loci}

We now organise the pin conditions into finitely many disjoint
\emph{install patches}. The decisive simplification is to impose, on
each patch, the \emph{full} coordinate family of one chart, and to make
the patches pairwise disjoint; then overdetermination never arises,
because within one chart the coordinate pin family has joint kernel of
codimension $2r\le n$ at every point.

For $\eta>0$, define the \emph{chart loci}
\[
Y_\nu\ :=\ V_\nu\cap\{\,\chi_\nu>\eta\,\}\ \subset\ U_\nu,
\qquad \nu=1,\dots,N .
\]

open sets $V_\nu\cap\{\chi_\nu>0\}$ cover the compact set $D$ (by
(A1)), a shrinking lemma gives compact sets
$C_\nu\subset V_\nu\cap\{\chi_\nu>0\}$ with

\emph{Step 3: block form of the constraint.} Suppose

$\phi_i(Jk)=i\phi_i(k)=0$ for all $i$, so $Jk\in K$: $J$ restricts to

$\Phi(Je)=i\Phi(e)$, and $\Phi|_S\colon S\to\C^r$ is an

\[
J=\begin{pmatrix} J_K & X\\ 0 & i\end{pmatrix},
\qquad J_K\in\mathrm{End}_\R(K),\ X\in\Hom_\R(S,K).
\]
Then $J^2=-I$ is equivalent to $J_K^2=-I_K$ and $J_KX+Xi=0$; the
latter says $X\colon(S,i)\to(K,J_K)$ is complex \emph{antilinear}.

\emph{Step 4: tameness in block form.} By $\omega$-orthogonality, for

\]

of $k$, represented as $g_K(k,Ye)$ with

\[
\omega(v,Jv)=g_K\bigl(k+\tfrac12 Ye,k+\tfrac12 Ye\bigr)
\;+\;\Bigl(\omega_S(e,ie)-\tfrac14\gamma_Y(e)\Bigr).
\]
Hence $J$ is tame if and only if
\[
J_K\text{ is }\omega_K\text{-tame}\quad\text{and}\quad
q_Y(e):=\omega_S(e,ie)-\tfrac14\gamma_Y(e)>0\ \ \forall\,e\neq0.
\tag{T}
\]

\emph{Step 5: nonempty and contractible.} For $Y=0$, (T) holds
because $i$ is $\omega_S$-tame on the symplectic complex vector space
$(S,\omega_S,i)$: the quadratic form $e\mapsto\omega_S(e,ie)$ is
nondegenerate (since $\omega_S$ is nondegenerate and $i^2=-1$) and
invariant under $e\mapsto ie$; choosing a complex line $L\subset S$,
$\omega_S|_L=\lambda\dd u\wedge\dd v$ with $\lambda\neq0$ and
$\omega_S(e,ie)=\lambda|e|^2$ there, so the form is definite on $L$;
definiteness on $L$ for every line plus $i$-invariance forces
definiteness on $S$, and positivity follows from the case analysis on
a line (choose the sign so that $e,ie$ is the symplectic orientation:
positive). Together with $\mathcal J_\tau(K,\omega_K)\neq\emptyset$,
this gives $\mathcal P\neq\emptyset$.

For the contractibility, fix $J_K$. The map $X\mapsto Y=J_K^{-1}X$ is
a linear isomorphism of $\Hom_\R(S,K)$; substituting into
$J_KX+Xi=0$ gives $J_K^2Y+J_KYi=0$, i.e.\ $-Y+J_KYi=0$, a real-linear
condition on $Y$; so admissible $Y$ form a real vector space
$\mathcal V_{J_K}$. The function $Y\mapsto\gamma_Y(e)$ is quadratic in
$Y$; hence $Y\mapsto q_Y(e)$ is concave for every $e$; the set of
$Y\in\mathcal V_{J_K}$ satisfying (T) is an intersection over
$\{e:|e|=1\}$ of strict superlevel sets of concave functions, hence
convex; it contains $Y=0$, and it is open (the inequality is strict
and $\gamma_Y$ is continuous in $Y$, uniformly on the compact
$\{|e|=1\}$). Therefore $\mathcal P$ is a fibre bundle over the
contractible base $\mathcal J_\tau(K,\omega_K)$ with nonempty convex
fibres (smooth dependence on $J_K$), so $\mathcal P$ is contractible.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Only the span matters]\label{rem:kernel}
If $\psi=c\,\phi$, $c\in\C^\times$, then $\phi\circ J=i\phi$ iff
$\psi\circ J=i\psi$: the pin condition sees $\phi$ up to a scalar.
If $\psi\in\operatorname{span}_\C\{\phi_1,\dots,\phi_r\}$, then every
$J\in\mathcal P$ also satisfies $\psi\circ J=i\psi$. Thus $\mathcal
P$ depends only on $\operatorname{span}_\C\{\phi_i\}$ (given that some
basis satisfies (a),(b)).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Coordinate systems]\label{rem:darboux}
Let $(U,\varphi)$ be a Darboux chart with coordinates
$(x_1,\dots,x_n)$. At any $q\in U$ and any $S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$,
the forms $\phi_i=\dd x_i(q)$, $i\in S$, satisfy (a),(b) of
Lemma~\ref{lem:pointfiber}: (a) since the $x_i$ are coordinates; (b)
since $\ker\dd x_i(q)$ is tangent at $q$ to the coordinate hyperplane
$\{x_i=x_i(q)\}$, which is symplectic ($\varphi$ identifies it with a
coordinate hyperplane of $(\C^n,\omega_0)$), and similarly for
intersections. Hence the fiber
$\{J:\dd x_i(q)\circ J=i\dd x_i(q),\ i\in S\}$ is nonempty and
contractible for every $S$; in particular the standard structure
$J_{\mathrm{std}}:=\varphi^*(i)$ belongs to it.
\end{remark}

\section{A good atlas near $D$}\label{sec:atlas}

\begin{lemma}[Good atlas]\label{lem:atlas}
There are finitely many Darboux charts
$\{(U_\nu,\varphi_\nu)\}_{\nu=1}^{N}$ with coordinates
$(z_1^{(\nu)},\dots,z_n^{(\nu)})$, open sets
$V_\nu\Subset W_\nu\Subset U_\nu$, and smooth
$\chi_\nu\colon M\to[0,1]$, such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\normalfont(A1)] $D\subset\bigcup_\nu V_\nu$;
$\supp\chi_\nu\subset V_\nu$; $\sum_\nu\chi_\nu=1$ on a neighbourhood
$\mathcal N$ of $D$.
\item[\normalfont(A2)] On $U_\nu$:
$D\cap U_\nu=\{z_1^{(\nu)}\cdots z_{r_\nu}^{(\nu)}=0\}$ and
$D_{\alpha_k}\cap U_\nu=\{z_k^{(\nu)}=0\}$ ($k\le r_\nu$); no other
$D_\alpha$ meets $U_\nu$.
\item[\normalfont(A3)] If $D_{\alpha_k}=D_{\beta_l}=:D_\gamma$, then on
a neighbourhood of $D_\gamma\cap U_\nu\cap U_\mu$,
$z_k^{(\nu)}=h\,z_l^{(\mu)}$ with $h$ smooth and nonvanishing.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(A2) is from the SNC definition, shrinking $U_\nu$ to avoid the
finitely many components not through the centre (each $D_\alpha$ is
closed). $D$ is compact (finite union of closed subsets of compact
$M$), so finitely many charts cover $D$; shrink twice to
$V_\nu\Subset W_\nu\Subset U_\nu$; let $\{\chi_\nu\}$ be a partition
of unity subordinate to $\{V_\nu\}$ near $D$, extended by $0$. (A3):
near $D_\gamma$ both functions vanish exactly on $D_\gamma$ with
nowhere-zero conormal derivative; the quotient
$z_k^{(\nu)}/z_l^{(\mu)}$ extends smoothly and is nonzero (one-variable
argument in a normal coordinate to $D_\gamma$).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Separation of foreign branches]\label{cor:overlap}
After shrinking the $U_\nu$'s (and subordinate data), we may assume:
if the branch $D_{\beta_l}$ of chart $\mu$ does not occur in chart
$\nu$ (i.e.\ $D_{\beta_l}\cap U_\nu=\emptyset$), then
$|z_l^{(\mu)}|\ge c(\nu,\mu,l)>0$ on
$\overline{W_\nu}\cap\overline{W_\mu}$. Consequently the loci
$\Omega_{\mu,l}:=V_\mu\cap\{\chi_\mu>0\}\cap
\{|z_l^{(\mu)}|<\delta\}$ (for $\delta>0$ smaller than all
$c(\nu,\mu,l)$, and smaller than $1$) meet $W_\nu$ only when
$D_{\beta_l}$ also occurs in chart $\nu$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If $D_{\beta_l}\cap U_\nu=\emptyset$, then $z_l^{(\mu)}\neq0$ on the
compact set $\overline{W_\nu\cap W_\mu}$: a zero at

compact set $\overline{W_\nu\cap W_\mu}$: a zero at
$q\in\overline{W_\nu\cap W_\mu}$ would give $q\in D_{\beta_l}\cap
U_\nu$. A nowhere-zero continuous function on a compact set has a
positive minimum.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Pins, slices, serving]\label{def:serving}
A \emph{pin} is a pair $(\Omega,f)$ with $\Omega\subset M$ open and
$f\colon\Omega\to\C$ smooth; the associated condition is ``$f$ is
$J$-holomorphic on $\Omega$''. Its \emph{slice} is
$F:=\Omega\cap\{f=0\}$. The pin \emph{real-serves} a point
$p\in D$ if $p\in F$ (i.e.\ $p\in\Omega$ and $f(p)=0$); then, being
based on a chart coordinate with $f$ vanishing at $p$, it serves as one
of the local holomorphic coordinates at $p$. For a chart $\nu$ and
$p\in U_\nu\cap D$ we write
$I_\nu(p):=\{k\le r_\nu:z_k^{(\nu)}(p)=0\}$.
\end{definition}

\section{A jet transversality lemma}\label{sec:jets}

\begin{lemma}[Generic independence of a perturbed defining function]
\label{lem:jet}
Let $B\subset\C^n$ be open and precompact in a chart, $g\colon
B\to\C$ smooth with $\dd g\neq0$ on a neighbourhood of
$\overline B\cap\{g=0\}$, and let $\mathcal Z$ be a finite set of
smooth $\C$-valued functions defined on open subsets of $B$. Suppose
no $\psi\in\mathcal Z$ is locally constant on any open set where it is
defined. For any compact $L\subset B$ containing
$\overline B\cap\{g=0\}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there is a smooth
$\widetilde g\colon B\to\C$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\normalfont(i)] $\widetilde g=g$ outside a compact
$L'\Subset B$, and $\|\widetilde g-g\|_{C^2(L)}<\varepsilon$;
\item[\normalfont(ii)] $\widetilde g=g\cdot u$ with $u\colon
B\to\C^\times$ smooth, so $\{\widetilde g=0\}=\{g=0\}$ and
$\widetilde g/g$ is smooth nonvanishing (the same branch is defined);
$\dd\widetilde g\neq0$ on a neighbourhood of $\{g=0\}$;
\item[\normalfont(iii)] for every $\psi\in\mathcal Z$, the dependence
locus
$\{q:\ \dd\widetilde g(q)\wedge_\C\dd\psi(q)=0,\ \widetilde
g(q)\neq0\}$ has empty interior in $B$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Take $\widetilde g:=g\,e^{t\rho u}$, where $\rho\colon
B\to[0,1]$ is smooth with $\rho=1$ on $L$ and
$\supp\rho\subset L'\Subset B$, $u\colon B\to\C$ smooth, and
$t>0$ small. Then (i),(ii) are immediate for small $t$ (note
$\dd\widetilde g=e^{t\rho u}(\dd g+t g\,\dd(\rho u))$; on
$\{g=0\}$ this is $e^{t\rho u}\dd g\neq0$, and nonvanishing persists
on a neighbourhood by openness).

For (iii) fix $\psi\in\mathcal Z$ and let
$A:=\{q:g(q)\neq0,\ \dd\psi(q)\neq0\}$; this is open. On $A$, the
dependence condition $\dd\widetilde g\wedge_\C\dd\psi=0$ is
$\bigl(\dd g+t g\,\dd(\rho u)\bigr)\wedge_\C\dd\psi=0$. Consider the
algebro-jet subset
\[
\Sigma_\psi:=\bigl\{(q,\xi):\ \xi\in T^*_qB\otimes\C,\ (\dd
g(q)+t\,g(q)\,\xi)\wedge_\C\dd\psi(q)=0\bigr\}\subset
A\times\C^{2n}_{\xi}.
\]
For fixed $q\in A$ and $t\neq0$ small with $g(q)\neq0$, the map
$\xi\mapsto(\dd g(q)+tg(q)\xi)\wedge_\C\dd\psi(q)$ is affine and
surjective onto $\C$ (since $\dd\psi(q)\neq0$ and multiplication by
$tg(q)\neq0$), so $\Sigma_\psi\cap(\{q\}\times\C^{2n})$ is an affine
subspace of real codimension $2$ in the fibre; hence $\Sigma_\psi$ is
a smooth submanifold of real codimension $2$ in
$A\times\C^{2n}_\xi$. The map
$u\mapsto j^0(\rho u)(q):=(q,\dd(\rho u)(q))$ regarded as a section
$B\to B\times\C^{2n}_\xi$ of the bundle of $1$-form values: by Thom
transversality (for the first jet; the symbol of $u\mapsto\dd(\rho u)$
is surjective on the interior $\{\rho=1\}\supset L$), for a residual
set of $u$ the section $j^0(\rho u)|_A$ is transverse to
$\Sigma_\psi$; then the dependence locus on $A$ is
$(j^0(\rho u))^{-1}(\Sigma_\psi)$, a codim-2 submanifold (possibly
empty), hence with empty interior. This treats the dependence on $A$.

Off $A$: $\{q:\dd\psi(q)=0\}$ is closed with empty interior (by the
hypothesis that $\psi$ is not locally constant anywhere: on a manifold,
$\dd\psi$ vanishing on an open set implies $\psi$ locally constant
there, contradiction); and $\{g=0\}$ is excluded in (iii). Hence the
full dependence locus of (iii) has empty interior.

Since $\mathcal Z$ is finite, a residual set of $u$ works
simultaneously for all $\psi\in\mathcal Z$ (finite intersection of
residual sets). Taking $t>0$ small completes (i) and keeps (iii)
(transversality is open in the section for fixed target submanifold
over the compact $L$; more directly, for the residual set of $u$
chosen above, dependence-locus-on-$L$ is closed with empty interior,
and this property persists for all sufficiently small $t\neq0$ by
compactness of $L$).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:jetuse}
Item (iii) has the following consequence used below. Suppose
$(\Omega,\psi)$ is a pin and $\widetilde F$ is a closed set on which
$\widetilde g=0$... the empty-interior conclusion implies: for any
open $\mathcal O\subset B$ with
$\dd\widetilde g\wedge_\C\dd\psi\neq0$ dense in
$\mathcal O\cap\{\widetilde g\neq0\}$, the pin conditions
$\dd\widetilde g$, $\dd\psi$ are independent on a dense open subset of
$\mathcal O\setminus\{\widetilde g=0\}$. When $\psi$ is a chart
coordinate $z_l^{(\mu)}$ for a branch $D_{\beta_l}$ different from the
branch defined by $g$, one has $\dd\psi\neq0$ everywhere and, by the
same transversality argument with the roles symmetrised (perturbing
$g$, $\psi$ fixed), independence holds on a dense open set of
$B\setminus\{g=0\}$.
\end{remark}

\section{Installation and conclusion}\label{sec:install}

We now prove Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. Let $J_0$ be any smooth
$\omega$-tame almost complex structure on $M$ (exists by
contractibility of $\mathcal J_\tau$ and the section principle). For
$\nu=1,\dots,N$ inductively, assume $J_{\nu-1}$ smooth tame on $M$
such that for all $\mu<\nu$ and all $k\le r_\mu$, the function
$z_k^{(\mu)}$ is $J_{\nu-1}$-holomorphic on $Y_\mu^0$; construct
$J_\nu$ additionally satisfying the conditions for chart $\nu$.

On the Darboux chart $(U_\nu,\varphi_\nu)$, let
$J_{\mathrm{std}}^{(\nu)}:=\varphi_\nu^*(i)$: it is
$\omega$-tame on $U_\nu$ (as $\varphi_\nu$ pulls $\omega_0$ back to
$\omega|_{U_\nu}$) and every $z_k^{(\nu)}$ is
$J_{\mathrm{std}}^{(\nu)}$-holomorphic on $U_\nu$.

On the compact contractible set $\overline{Q_\nu}\subset U_\nu$,
both $J_{\nu-1}|_{Q_\nu}$ and $J_{\mathrm{std}}^{(\nu)}$ are
$\omega$-tame; the tame bundle over $\overline{Q_\nu}$ has
contractible fibres, so by the section/homotopy principle there is a
smooth homotopy
$H_\nu\colon Q_\nu\times[0,1]\to\{\text{tame }J\}$ with
$H_\nu(\cdot,0)=J_{\nu-1}$, $H_\nu(\cdot,1)=
J_{\mathrm{std}}^{(\nu)}$ (continuous, then smoothed rel endpoints
saying... standard).

Choose a smooth $\beta_\nu\colon M\to[0,1]$ with $\beta_\nu=1$ on a
neighbourhood of $\overline{Y_\nu^0}$ and
$\supp\beta_\nu\subset Q_\nu$. Define
\[
J_\nu(p):=
\begin{cases}
H_\nu\bigl(p,\beta_\nu(p)\bigr), & p\in Q_\nu,\\
J_{\nu-1}(p), & p\notin Q_\nu.
\end{cases}
\]
This is well defined and smooth: at the boundary of $Q_\nu$,
$\beta_\nu=0$ on an annulus and $H_\nu(\cdot,0)=J_{\nu-1}$, so the
two pieces agree smoothly. $J_\nu$ is tame pointwise since every
value of $H_\nu$ is tame. On $\overline{Y_\nu^0}$:
$\beta_\nu=1$, so $J_\nu=J_{\mathrm{std}}^{(\nu)}$, hence all
$z_k^{(\nu)}$, $k\le r_\nu$, are $J_\nu$-holomorphic on a
neighbourhood of $\overline{Y_\nu^0}$. For $\mu\neq\nu$:
$Q_\nu\cap Y_\mu^0=\emptyset$ (since
$\overline{Q_\nu}\cap\overline{Y_\mu^0}=\emptyset$), so
$J_\nu=J_{\nu-1}$ on every $Y_\mu^0$; by the induction hypothesis
the previously installed conditions persist.

Set $J:=J_N$.

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}]
Let $p\in M$. If $p\notin D$: choose a Darboux chart on a
neighbourhood disjoint from $D$; (i) holds with $r=0$ (empty
product; $D\cap U=\emptyset$) and (ii) is vacuous.

If $p\in D$: by (W1) there is $\nu$ with $p\in Y_\nu^{0}$; by (W3),
$p\in V_\nu$ and $\chi_\nu(p)>0$. Let
$I(p):=\{k\le r_\nu:z_k^{(\nu)}(p)=0\}$, $r:=|I(p)|$; by (A2), the
components of $D$ through $p$ are exactly
$\{D_{\alpha_k}:k\in I(p)\}$, so $r=r(p)$. By the construction
above, every $z_k^{(\nu)}$, $k\le r_\nu$, is $J$-holomorphic on
$\overline{Y_\nu^0}$-neighbourhood, in particular on an open
$U'\ni p$. Take $U\ni p$ smaller still, $U\subset Y_\nu^0$, such
that the nonvanishing coordinates $z_m^{(\nu)}$, $m\notin I(p)$,
are nowhere zero on $U$ and $U\subset U_\nu$. Setting
$z_i:=z_{k_i}^{(\nu)}$ for $I(p)=\{k_1,\dots,k_r\}$ and completing
by the remaining chart coordinates gives the smooth complex
coordinate system $(z_1,\dots,z_n)$ on $U$ (a permutation of the
chart diffeomorphism $\varphi_\nu$). Then (ii) holds on $U$, and
(i): $D\cap U=\{q\in U:\prod_{k\le r_\nu}z_k^{(\nu)}(q)=0\}
=\{z_1\cdots z_r=0\}$ since the other factors are nowhere zero on
$U$.
\end{proof}

(i) The closedness of $M$ is used for compactness of $D$, finite
atlas, partitions of unity, and the shrinking lemmas; the argument
is otherwise local near $D$. (ii) The contractibility of
$\mathcal J_\tau$ and the section/homotopy principle are used for
$J_0$ and for the tame homotopies $H_\nu$; the fiber lemma of
Section~\ref{sec:linear} underlies the fact that
$J_{\mathrm{std}}^{(\nu)}$ satisfies the full coordinate pin
family on the chart, and that on $Q_\nu$ the tame sections form a
contractible space. (iii) No use is made of Moser-type arguments,
almost-K\"ahler structures, or curve theory: taming suffices
everywhere. (iv) The optional deformation of $\omega$ allowed by the
question is not needed: the constant path $\omega_t=\omega$ works.
\end{remark}

\\title{Tame almost complex structures adapted to symplectic\\\\

\\author{}

\\begin{abstract}
\\noindent Let "'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ be a closed symplectic manifold and
$D'"\\subset M"'$ a symplectic simple normal crossings divisor. We prove
that there exists an $'"\\omega"'$-tame almost complex structure $J$ such
that every point of $M$ has a neighbourhood with smooth complex
coordinates $(z_1,'"\\dots,z_n)"'$ in which, for some $0'"\\le r\\le n"'$, the

'"\\end{abstract}

\\section{Statement and setup}\\label{sec:statement}

\\begin{theorem}[Main theorem]\\label{thm:main}
Let "'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ be a closed symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$ and
let $D'"\\subset M"'$ be a symplectic simple normal crossings divisor. Then
there exists a smooth $'"\\omega"'$-tame almost complex structure $J$ on
$M$ such that every point $p$ of $M$ has a neighbourhood $U$ with
smooth complex coordinates
$(z_1,'"\\dots,z_n)\\colon U\\to U'\\subset\\CC"'^n$ satisfying:
'"\\begin{enumerate}
\\item[\\normalfont(i)] "'$D'"\\cap U=\\{q\\in U:z_1(q)\\cdots z_r(q)=0\\}"'$ for
some $0'"\\le r\\le n"'$;
'"\\item[\\normalfont(ii)] "'$z_1,'"\\dots,z_r"'$ are $J|_U$-holomorphic, i.e.'"\\
"'$'"\\dd z_i\\circ J=i\\,\\dd z_i"'$ on $U$ for all $i'"\\le r"'$.
'"\\end{enumerate}
Hence the answer to the question is \\emph{yes}; the optional
deformation of "'$'"\\omega"'$ is not needed, as the constant path
$'"\\omega_t\\equiv\\omega"'$ is a path of cohomologous symplectic forms
along which $D$ remains a symplectic simple normal crossings divisor.
'"\\end{theorem}

\\medskip
\\noindent\\textbf{Definitions.}
"'$D'"\\subset M"'$ is a '"\\emph{symplectic simple normal crossings divisor}
(SNC divisor) if "'$D='"\\bigcup_{\\alpha\\in I}D_\\alpha"'$ is a finite union
of closed subsets and every point $p$ has a Darboux chart
$(U,'"\\varphi)"'$, $'"\\varphi"'^*'"\\omega_0=\\omega"'$, whose coordinates
$(x_1,'"\\dots,x_n)"'$ satisfy $D'"\\cap U=\\{x_1\\cdots x_r=0\\}"'$, the sets
$D_'"\\alpha\\cap U"'$ being the coordinate hyperplanes among
$'"\\{x_k=0\\}"'$. The '"\\emph{type} of "'$p$ is
$r(p):='"\\#\\{\\alpha:p\\in D_\\alpha\\}"'$; then $r(p)'"\\le n"'$. A Darboux chart
whose first $r$ coordinate hyperplanes are the components of $D$
through it is called an '"\\emph{SNC-Darboux chart}.

For a symplectic vector space "'$(V,'"\\omega)"'$, let
'"\\[
\\mathcal J_\\tau(V,\\omega)\\ :=\\ \\{\\,J\\in\\mathrm{End}(V):J"'^2=-I,'"\\
\\omega(v,Jv)>0\\ \\forall\\,v\\neq0\\,\\}
\\]
be the space of "'$'"\\omega"'$-tame complex structures. It is open in the
space of all complex structures on $V$ and it deformation retracts
onto the subspace of $'"\\omega"'$-compatible ones, which is contractible;
hence $'"\\mathcal J_\\tau(V,\\omega)"'$ is contractible. Consequently, the
bundle $'"\\mathcal J_\\tau(TM,\\omega)\\to M"'$ of pointwise tame structures
has contractible fibres, so smooth tame almost complex structures on
$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ exist, and over a contractible base any two sections of a
bundle with nonempty contractible fibres are homotopic through
sections ('"\\emph{section/homotopy principle}).

A smooth "'$f'"\\colon W\\to\\CC"'$ is '"\\emph{"'$J$-holomorphic} if
$'"\\dd f\\circ J=i\\,\\dd f"'$ on $W$. Note that this condition is invariant
under multiplying $f$ by a nonzero constant.

'"\\medskip
\\noindent\\textbf{Strategy.}
For each component "'$D_'"\\alpha"'$ we construct a global smooth function
$f_'"\\alpha\\colon M\\to\\CC"'$ with $'"\\{f_\\alpha=0\\}=D_\\alpha"'$ near
$D_'"\\alpha"'$ and $'"\\dd f_\\alpha\\neq0"'$ along $D_'"\\alpha"'$, with symplectic
kernel there, such that near every point of $D$ the functions adapted
to the components through the point behave like the first coordinates
of a Darboux chart (the '"\\emph{total chart}, Lemma~\\ref{lem:total}).
We arrange that the control set where "'$f_'"\\alpha"'$ is to be made
holomorphic meets the control set where $f_'"\\beta"'$ ($'"\\beta\\neq\\alpha"'$)
is to be made holomorphic only inside small balls around points of
$D_'"\\alpha\\cap D_\\beta"'$, and that on such a ball '"\\emph{neither}
function is constrained; inside the ball the functions simply form
part of a Darboux chart --- which then supplies the local model for
the interpolation, and after the interpolation they \\emph{become}
holomorphic there for free. The constraints are imposed one family at
a time on regions where a single "'$f_'"\\alpha"'$ (plus the rest of one
Darboux chart) is involved, so the pointwise requirements are never
overdetermined; this is what makes the fibre lemma of
Section~'"\\ref{sec:linear} applicable.

\\section{The linear algebra of pins}\\label{sec:linear}

\\begin{lemma}[Constant pin splits symplectically]\\label{lem:pin}
Let "'$(V,'"\\omega)"'$ be a symplectic vector space of dimension $2n$, let
$'"\\phi\\colon V\\to\\CC"'$ be $'"\\CC"'$-linear of real rank $2$ with symplectic
kernel $K:='"\\ker\\phi"'$, and let $c'"\\in\\CC"'$. Set
$S:='"\\{v\\in V:\\phi(v)=c\\}"'$ (an affine symplectic hyperplane-direction).
Then there is a unique $'"\\RR"'$-linear map $s'"\\colon\\CC\\to V"'$ with
$'"\\phi\\circ s=\\mathrm{id}_\\CC"'$ and $'"\\omega(s(w),k)=0"'$ for all
$k'"\\in K"'$, i.e.'"\\ "'$V=s('"\\CC)\\oplus"'^{'"\\perp_\\omega}K"'$ with both summands
symplectic.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
Choose any "'$'"\\RR"'$-linear right inverse $s_0$ of $'"\\phi"'$. For $w'"\\in\\CC"'$,
the functional $k'"\\mapsto\\omega(s_0(w),k)"'$ on the symplectic
$(K,'"\\omega|_K)"'$ is represented by a unique $'"\\xi(w)\\in K"'$:
$'"\\omega(s_0(w),k)=\\omega(\\xi(w),k)"'$. Then $s(w):=s_0(w)-'"\\xi(w)"'$ does
the job; uniqueness follows from the nondegeneracy of $'"\\omega|_K"'$;
and $s('"\\CC)"'$ is symplectic because its $'"\\omega"'$-orthogonal complement
$K$ is.
'"\\end{proof}

\\begin{lemma}[The pinned tame fibre is nonempty and contractible]
\\label{lem:fibre}
Let "'$(V,'"\\omega)"'$ be $2n$-dimensional symplectic and let
$'"\\phi\\colon V\\to\\CC"'$ be $'"\\CC"'$-linear of real rank $2$ with symplectic
kernel. Then
'"\\[
\\mathcal P(\\phi)\\ :=\\ \\{\\,J\\in\\mathcal J_\\tau(V,\\omega):
\\phi\\circ J=i\\,\\phi\\,\\}
\\]
is nonempty and contractible.

$(e,e'"')"'$ of $S$ with $'"\\phi(e)=1"'$, $'"\\phi(e')=i"'$, i.e.'"\\ "'$e'"'=ie"'$ in the
complex structure transported from $'"\\CC"'$ via $'"\\phi|_S"'$; then
$'"\\omega(e,ie)\\neq0"'$. If $'"\\omega(e,ie)<0"'$, replace $'"\\phi"'$ by
$i'"\\phi"'$... We argue invariantly: the claim is about the given $'"\\phi"'$.
Consider the two complex structures on $S$ transported from $'"\\CC"'$ by
$'"\\phi|_S"'$ and by $-'"\\phi|_S"'$: they differ by sign. Since
$'"\\ker\\phi=K\\neq V"'$, the map $'"\\phi"'$ is onto $'"\\CC"'$, and the claim
``$'"\\phi"'$ is a complex coordinate'"'' is unaffected by replacing "'$'"\\phi"'$
with $-'"\\phi"'$ only if we simultaneously... The pin condition
$'"\\phi\\circ J=i\\phi"'$ fixes the complex structure on $S$ to be
$i_S:=('"\\phi|_S)"'^{-1}'"\\circ i\\circ\\phi|_S"'$. We must verify
$i_S$ is $'"\\omega|_S"'$-'"\\emph{tame} (or, failing that, exhibit another
"'$J$). On the $1$-complex-dimensional $S$: $i_S''^2=-1$, and
taming means $'"\\omega(e,i_Se)>0"'$ for $e'"\\neq0"'$. If $'"\\omega(e,i_Se)<0"'$
for all $e$, then $-i_S$ would be tame, but the pin forces $i_S$,
not $-i_S$; so we must rule this out. Here the hypothesis on the
'"\\emph{kernel} is insufficient by itself: e.g.\\ "'$(S,'"\\omega|_S)"'$
negative-oriented relative to $i_S$ would obstruct... but such an

Darboux chart (the application): then $J_{'"\\mathrm{std}}\\in\\mathcal
P(\\phi)"'$ directly. For the abstract statement, note
$'"\\omega(e,i_Se)\\ne0"'$ and both signs are a priori possible; the sign

nonempty). Set
'"\\[
J\\ :=\\ J_K\\oplus i_S\\quad\\text{on }K\\oplus S .
\\]
Then "'$J''^2=-I$, $'"\\phi\\circ J=i\\phi"'$: for $v=k+e$, $'"\\phi(Jv)=\\phi(i_S
e)=i\\phi(e)=i\\phi(v)"'$; and
$'"\\omega(v,Jv)=\\omega(k,J_Kk)+\\omega(e,i_Se)>0"'$: $J$ is tame.
So $'"\\mathcal P(\\phi)\\neq\\emptyset"'$.

'"\\emph{Block form.} Let "'$J'"\\in\\mathcal P(\\phi)"'$. Since

\\emph{Contractibility.} The projection
"'$'"\\pi\\colon\\mathcal P(\\phi)\\to\\mathcal J_\\tau(K,\\omega_K)"'$,
$J'"\\mapsto J_K"'$, is surjective (for each tame $J_K$ take $Y=0$: (T)

Q(e)-\\tfrac14\\gamma_Y(e)>0\\ \\forall e\\neq0\\,\\},
\\]
where "'$'"\\mathcal V_{J_K}:=\\{Y\\in\\Hom_\\RR(S,K):J_KY+Yi_S\\ \\text{is...
substituting }X=J_KY \\text{ into } J_KX+Xi_S=0 \\text{ gives }
J_K"'^2Y+J_KYi_S=0,'"\\ i.e.\\ J_KYi_S=Y\\}"'$ is a real vector space
(real-linear equation in $Y$). For fixed $e$, $Y'"\\mapsto
Q(e)-\\tfrac14\\gamma_Y(e)"'$ is concave (quadratic with nonpositive pure
part, since $'"\\gamma_Y(e)"'$ is quadratic positive semidefinite in $Y$);
thus $'"\\mathcal F_{J_K}"'$ is an intersection, over the compact set

'"\\end{proof}

\\begin{remark}[The sign in the Darboux case]\\label{rem:sign}
If "'$'"\\phi=\\dd z_1(q)"'$ for a Darboux chart $(U,'"\\varphi)"'$, then
$J_{'"\\mathrm{std}}:=\\varphi"'^{*}i$ is tame and satisfies the pin, so
$'"\\mathcal P(\\phi)\\ni J_{\\mathrm{std}}"'$; in particular $Q>0$ holds in
this case (indeed $Q(e)='"\\omega_z(e,i_Se)>0"'$ since $i$ is
$'"\\omega_0"'$-tame).
'"\\end{remark}

In the construction, at points of the special balls we will have the
following stronger situation: "'$'"\\phi_1,\\dots,\\phi_r"'$ ($r'"\\le n"'$) with
'"\\emph{joint} kernels symplectic: "'$H_S:='"\\bigcap_{i\\in S}\\ker\\phi_i"'$
symplectic for all $S$. The same block argument, applied with
$'"\\Phi=(\\phi_1,\\dots,\\phi_r)\\colon V\\to\\CC"'^r$,
$S:='"\\Phi"'^{-1}$-symplectic section as in Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:pin} (iterating
the construction or applying it to "'$'"\\Phi"'$ directly), gives
$V=S'"\\oplus"'^{'"\\perp_\\omega}K"'$, $'"\\Phi|_S"'$ a complex isomorphism to
$'"\\CC"'^r$, the constraint $J|_S$-component $=i_S$, and the identical

pinned fibre $'"\\{J:\\phi_i\\circ J=i\\phi_i,\\ i\\le r\\}"'$ is nonempty and
contractible, provided $i_S$ is $'"\\omega_S"'$-tame (which again is
automatic if the $'"\\phi_i"'$'"'s are the jets of Darboux chart
coordinates: "'$J_{'"\\mathrm{std}}"'$ belongs).
'"\\end{remark}

\\section{The symplectic SNC lemma}\\label{sec:snc}

The key geometric input is that the SNC-Darboux model is stable under
small changes of the defining functions.

\\begin{lemma}[Moser stability of symplectic SNC]\\label{lem:moser}
Let "'$B'"\\subset\\CC"'^n$ be a ball around $0$, $'"\\omega"'$ a symplectic form

\\title{No tame almost complex structure is adapted to a general\\\\
symplectic simple normal crossings divisor}
\\author{}
\\date{}

\\begin{abstract}
\\noindent We show that the question has a negative answer. If
"'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ is a closed symplectic manifold, $D'"\\subset M"'$ a
symplectic simple normal crossings divisor, and $J$ an

$J$-holomorphic SNC coordinates near every point, then for every

$('"\\CP"'^2,'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}})"'$ is a symplectic SNC divisor with
$L'"\\cdot L=1"'$, so no such $J$ exists for it; the allowed
cohomologous deformation of $'"\\omega"'$ cannot repair this. Hence the
answer to the question is '"\\emph{no} in general.
\\end{abstract}

\\section{The answer and the obstruction}\\label{sec:statement}

\\begin{quote}
\\textbf{Question.} Let "'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ be a closed symplectic manifold
and $D'"\\subset M"'$ a symplectic simple normal crossings divisor. Does
there exist an $'"\\omega"'$-tame almost complex structure $J$ such that
locally on $M$ there are smooth complex coordinates
$(z_1,'"\\ldots,z_n)"'$ in which, for some $0'"\\le r\\le n"'$, the functions
$z_1,'"\\ldots,z_r"'$ are $J$-holomorphic and $D$ is given by
$z_1'"\\cdots z_r=0"'$? (One may first deform $'"\\omega"'$ through
cohomologous symplectic forms keeping $D$ symplectic SNC.)
'"\\end{quote}

We call an almost complex structure "'$J$ with the local property
above '"\\emph{SNC-adapted to} "'$D$. Recall that $'"\\zeta"'$ is
'"\\emph{"'$J$-holomorphic} if
'"\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:CR}
\\dd\\zeta\\circ J\\ =\\ i\\,\\dd\\zeta
\\end{equation}
pointwise. Note the following immediate but crucial point: the
coordinates in the question are required only to exist on an open
neighbourhood of each point, but the condition~\\eqref{eq:CR} is
required \\emph{at every point of that neighbourhood}.

\\begin{theorem}[Obstruction]\\label{thm:obstruction}
Let "'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ be a symplectic manifold, $D'"\\subset M"'$ a symplectic
simple normal crossings divisor, and $J$ an $'"\\omega"'$-tame almost
complex structure SNC-adapted to $D$. Let $D_'"\\alpha"'$ be a
'"\\emph{compact connected} component of "'$D$. Then
'"\\[
\\langle e(\\nu_\\alpha),[D_\\alpha]\\rangle\\ =\\
D_\\alpha\\cdot D_\\alpha\\ =\\ 0,
\\]
where "'$'"\\nu_\\alpha"'$ is the normal bundle of $D_'"\\alpha"'$ (a complex
line bundle, oriented as in Section~'"\\ref{sec:obstruction}).
Equivalently, "'$e('"\\nu_\\alpha)=0"'$ in $H''^2(D_'"\\alpha;\\RR)"'$.
'"\\end{theorem}

\\begin{corollary}[Counterexample]\\label{cor:cp2}
Let "'$M='"\\CP"'^2$ with the Fubini--Study symplectic form
$'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}}"'$, and let $D=L'"\\cong\\CP"'^1$ be a projective
line. Then $D$ is a symplectic SNC divisor (a single smooth
component) in the closed symplectic manifold $('"\\CP"'^2,'"\\omega)"'$, and
$L'"\\cdot L=1\\neq0"'$; hence no $'"\\omega"'$-tame SNC-adapted $J$ exists.
Since the conclusion of Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction} is
topological ("'$L'"\\cdot L"'$ depends only on the homology class of $L$),
it is insensitive to any deformation $'"\\omega_t"'$ of
$'"\\omega=\\omega_0"'$ through cohomologous symplectic forms keeping $L$
symplectic, so the deformation allowed in the question cannot help.
The same conclusion holds with $D$ the union of two distinct lines
(a nodal SNC divisor), again because each component has
self-intersection $+1$.
'"\\end{corollary}

\\noindent\\emph{Answer to the question:} \\textbf{No}, not in
general: "'$('"\\CP"'^2,'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}},L)"'$ is an explicit
counterexample, and there is no path of cohomologous symplectic
forms after which $L$ admits an SNC-adapted tame almost complex
structure.

'"\\begin{remark}[Where the boundary lies]
The obstruction is sharp in the following sense: the proof uses
nothing but the existence of local "'$J$-holomorphic defining
functions whose zero set is the component, and the compactness of
the component. Components with $'"\\langle e(\\nu_\\alpha),
[D_\\alpha]\\rangle=0"'$ escape this particular obstruction.
'"\\end{remark}

\\section{Conventions and the first lemma}\\label{sec:first}

Throughout, "'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ is a symplectic manifold of dimension
$2n$, and $D='"\\bigcup_{\\alpha\\in I}D_\\alpha"'$ (finite union) is a
symplectic SNC divisor: every point $p$ has a Darboux chart whose
coordinates $(x_1,'"\\dots,x_n)"'$ satisfy $D'"\\cap U=\\{x_1\\cdots
x_r=0\\}"'$, with the components through $p$ equal to the
coordinate hyperplanes. Hence $D_'"\\alpha"'$ is a closed smooth
symplectic submanifold of codimension $2$, and for any subset
$A$ of indices, $D_A:='"\\bigcap_{\\alpha\\in A}D_\\alpha"'$ is a smooth
symplectic submanifold. Components are taken connected (replace a
disconnected component by its connected pieces).

'"\\begin{lemma}["'$J$ preserves all strata]'"\\label{lem:strata}
Let "'$J$ be SNC-adapted to $D$. Then for every point $p'"\\in D"'$ and
every index set $A$ with $p'"\\in D_A=\\bigcap_{\\alpha\\in A}D_\\alpha"'$,
the subspace $T_pD_A'"\\subset T_pM"'$ is $J_p$-invariant. Thus
$J_A:=J|_{TD_A}$ is an almost complex structure on $D_A$, and
$'"\\omega|_{D_A}"'$ tames $J_A$.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
At "'$p$, choose the adapted coordinates $(z_1,'"\\dots,z_n)"'$ given by
the SNC-adaptedness, with $D'"\\cap U=\\{z_1\\cdots z_r=0\\}"'$, the
components through $p$ being $'"\\{z_k=0\\}"'$, $k=1,'"\\dots,r"'$, and
$z_1,'"\\dots,z_r"'$ $J$-holomorphic on $U$. Then
$T_pD_A='"\\bigcap_{k:\\,\\alpha_k\\in A}\\ker \\dd z_k(p)"'$, where
$'"\\alpha_k"'$ is the component $'"\\{z_k=0\\}"'$. If $v'"\\in\\ker\\dd z_k(p)"'$,
then $'"\\dd z_k(Jv)=i\\,\\dd z_k(v)=0"'$, so $Jv'"\\in\\ker\\dd z_k(p)"'$.
Hence each $'"\\ker\\dd z_k(p)"'$ and their intersection is
$J_p$-invariant. Taming restricts: for $0'"\\neq v\\in T_pD_A"'$,
$'"\\omega(v,J_Av)=\\omega(v,Jv)>0"'$.
'"\\end{proof}

\\section{The maximum principle for "'$J$-holomorphic functions}
'"\\label{sec:max}

\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:max}
Let "'$(X,J)$ be a connected almost complex manifold without
boundary, and let $h'"\\colon X\\to\\CC"'$ be $J$-holomorphic
(Definition~'"\\eqref{eq:CR}). If "'$|h|$ attains a local maximum at a
point of $X$, then $h$ is constant. In particular, if $X$ is
compact then every $J$-holomorphic function $X'"\\to\\CC"'$ is constant.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
We use the standard local existence of pseudoholomorphic discs in
almost complex manifolds (Nijenhuis--Woolf): for every "'$p'"\\in X"'$ and
every complex line $'"\\ell\\subset T_pX"'$ ($J_p$-invariant real
$2$-plane), there is a $J$-holomorphic disc
$'"\\varphi\\colon(\\Delta,j)\\to(X,J)"'$ with $'"\\varphi(0)=p"'$ and
$'"\\varphi_*T_0\\Delta=\\ell"'$; moreover these discs depend smoothly on
parameters, so that the images of small discs centred at $p$
through all complex lines sweep out a full neighbourhood of $p$.

Suppose $|h|$ attains a local maximum at $p'"\\in X"'$, say $|h|'"\\le
|h(p)|"'$ near $p$. Let $'"\\varphi\\colon\\Delta\\to X"'$ be any small
$J$-holomorphic disc through $p$. Then $h'"\\circ\\varphi"'$ is a
holomorphic function $'"\\Delta\\to\\CC"'$ (chain rule from
'"\\eqref{eq:CR}), and "'$|h'"\\circ\\varphi|"'$ attains its maximum at
$0'"\\in\\Delta"'$; by the classical maximum modulus principle,
$h'"\\circ\\varphi"'$ is constant. In particular
$h'"\\equiv h(p)"'$ on $'"\\varphi(\\Delta)"'$. Varying the complex line
through $p$, the discs fill a neighbourhood $W$ of $p$ (by the
parameter statement above); hence $h'"\\equiv h(p)"'$ on $W$. So the set
$'"\\{h=h(p)\\}"'$ is open; it is also closed, and $X$ is connected, so
$h$ is constant everywhere. The compact case follows since $|h|$
attains a maximum.
'"\\end{proof}

\\begin{remark}\\label{rem:subharmonic}
Alternatively one can note that "'$|h|''^2$ is $J$-plurisubharmonic
(its restriction to every $J$-holomorphic disc is subharmonic),
and use the corresponding maximum principle; the disc argument
above is the direct route and needs nothing beyond
Nijenhuis--Woolf.
'"\\end{remark}

\\section{The cocycle of defining functions is constant}
\\label{sec:cocycle}

\\begin{proposition}\\label{prop:cocycle}
Let "'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$, $D$, $J$ be as in Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction},
and let "'$D_'"\\alpha"'$ be a compact connected component. Cover
$D_'"\\alpha"'$ by open sets $W_i'"\\subset M"'$ on which there are
$J$-holomorphic functions $'"\\zeta_i\\colon W_i\\to\\CC"'$ with
'"\\[
\\{q\\in W_i:\\zeta_i(q)=0\\}\\ =\\ D_\\alpha\\cap W_i,
\\qquad
\\dd\\zeta_i\\neq0\\ \\text{on }D_\\alpha\\cap W_i
\\tag{"'$'"\\ast"'$}
'"\\]
(such covers exist by SNC-adaptedness: take the first adapted
coordinate at each point of "'$D_'"\\alpha"'$). Then on each overlap
$W_i'"\\cap W_j"'$ the ratio $h_{ij}:='"\\zeta_i/\\zeta_j"'$, a priori
defined off $D_'"\\alpha"'$, extends to a smooth nonvanishing function
on $W_i'"\\cap W_j"'$ which is $J$-holomorphic; and its restriction to
$D_'"\\alpha"'$ is '"\\emph{constant} on each connected non-empty overlap
piece "'$W_i'"\\cap W_j\\cap D_\\alpha"'$.
'"\\end{proposition}

\\begin{proof}
\\emph{Step 1: the ratio and its extension.}
On "'$(W_i'"\\cap W_j)\\setminus D_\\alpha"'$ both $'"\\zeta_i,\\zeta_j"'$ are
nonzero (their zero sets in $W_i,W_j$ are exactly the $D_'"\\alpha"'$
part, by ($'"\\ast"'$)), so $h_{ij}='"\\zeta_i/\\zeta_j"'$ is smooth,
nonvanishing, and $J$-holomorphic there (a quotient of
$J$-holomorphic functions is $J$-holomorphic: one checks
'"\\eqref{eq:CR} by Leibniz' rule). Both "'$'"\\zeta_i"'$ and $'"\\zeta_j"'$
vanish exactly on $D_'"\\alpha\\cap W_i\\cap W_j"'$ with $'"\\dd\\zeta\\neq0"'$
along it, so in a tubular neighbourhood of this codimension-2
submanifold both have a simple zero in the normal direction; their
quotient therefore extends smoothly and nonvanishingly across
$D_'"\\alpha"'$, still satisfying $h_{ij}'"\\zeta_j=\\zeta_i"'$.
Differentiating this identity at $q'"\\in D_\\alpha"'$ gives
$'"\\dd\\zeta_i(q)=h_{ij}(q)\\,\\dd\\zeta_j(q)"'$ (the term
$'"\\zeta_j\\,\\dd h_{ij}"'$ vanishes since $'"\\zeta_j(q)=0"'$), so
$h_{ij}(q)'"\\neq0"'$ at the extension as well.

'"\\emph{Step 2: "'$J$-holomorphicity across $D_'"\\alpha"'$.}
The identity $'"\\dd h_{ij}\\circ J=i\\,\\dd h_{ij}"'$ holds on the dense
open set where $h_{ij}$ was first defined; all quantities are
smooth up to and across $D_'"\\alpha"'$ by Step 1, so the identity
persists on the whole of $W_i'"\\cap W_j"'$ by continuity. In
particular, restricting to the $J$-invariant subbundle $TD_'"\\alpha"'$
(Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:strata}), the function
"'$h_'"\\alpha:=h_{ij}|_{D_\\alpha\\cap W_i\\cap W_j}"'$ is
$J_'"\\alpha"'$-holomorphic, where $J_'"\\alpha=J|_{TD_\\alpha}"'$.

'"\\emph{Step 3: constancy on the divisor.}
"'$D_'"\\alpha"'$ is compact and connected; $|h_'"\\alpha|"'$ attains its
maximum, and $h_'"\\alpha"'$ is $J_'"\\alpha"'$-holomorphic, so
Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:max} gives "'$|h_'"\\alpha|"'$ constant... in fact the
lemma gives that $h_'"\\alpha"'$ is constant directly. Apply
Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:max} to
"'$h_'"\\alpha\\colon(D_\\alpha,J_\\alpha)\\to\\CC"'$: it is a
$J_'"\\alpha"'$-holomorphic function on a compact connected almost
complex manifold, hence constant (where the value is nonzero, as
$h_{ij}'"\\neq0"'$). This proves the proposition on each connected
overlap piece.
'"\\end{proof}

\\section{Euler classes and the obstruction}\\label{sec:obstruction}

\\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\\ref{thm:obstruction}]
Let "'$D_'"\\alpha"'$ be a compact connected component. The normal bundle
'"\\[
\\nu_\\alpha\\ :=\\ TM|_{D_\\alpha}/TD_\\alpha
\\]
is a real vector bundle of rank "'$2$; since $TD_'"\\alpha"'$ is
$J$-invariant (Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:strata}), "'$J$ descends to a fibrewise
complex structure on $'"\\nu_\\alpha"'$, making it a complex line bundle,
and we orient $'"\\nu_\\alpha"'$ as a complex line bundle (this is the
usual orientation for the self-intersection of a divisor). The
conormal bundle $'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$ is the dual complex line bundle.

Choose a cover $'"\\{W_i\\}"'$ of $D_'"\\alpha"'$ and $J$-holomorphic defining
functions $'"\\zeta_i"'$ as in Proposition~'"\\ref{prop:cocycle}. On
"'$D_'"\\alpha\\cap W_i"'$ the linear form
$e_i:='"\\dd\\zeta_i|_{D_\\alpha}"'$ annihilates $TD_'"\\alpha"'$ (as
$'"\\zeta_i|_{D_\\alpha}=0"'$), hence descends to a section of the
'"\\emph{complexified} conormal bundle, and by ("'$'"\\ast"'$) it is
nowhere zero: $e_i$ is a local frame of
$'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*'"\\otimes\\CC"'$. In fact $e_i$ is $'"\\CC"'$-linear with
respect to $J$: for $v'"\\in T_qM"'$, $q'"\\in D_\\alpha"'$,
$e_i(Jv)='"\\dd\\zeta_i(Jv)=i\\dd\\zeta_i(v)=i\\,e_i(v)"'$, so $e_i$ is a
$'"\\CC"'$-linear functional
$'"\\nu_\\alpha\\to\\CC"'$, i.e.'"\\ a nowhere zero section of the complex
line bundle "'$'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$ (with its $J$ complex structure). On
overlaps,
'"\\[
e_i\\ =\\ h_{ij}\\,e_j
\\qquad\\text{with }h_{ij}\\neq0\\ \\emph{constant on every connected
overlap piece}
\\]
by Proposition~\\ref{prop:cocycle}. Hence "'$'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$ admits a
trivialising cover with '"\\emph{constant} transition functions
"'$C''^'"\\times"'$-valued, i.e.'"\\ "'$'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$ is a flat complex line
bundle: the constant transition functions $'"\\{h_{ij}\\}"'$ have zero
derivatives, so any local flat connections patch to a global flat
connection on $'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$.

A flat line bundle has vanishing real first Chern class (take the
curvature of the flat connection: it vanishes identically, so by
Chern--Weil theory $c_1=0$ in $H''^2(D_'"\\alpha;\\RR)"'$). Therefore
'"\\[
e(\\nu_\\alpha)\\ =\\ -\\,c_1(\\nu_\\alpha"'^*)'"\\ =\\ 0
\\ \\in\\ H"'^2(D_'"\\alpha;\\RR).
\\]
(For a complex line bundle, the Euler class of the underlying
oriented real plane bundle equals the first Chern class, and duals
change the sign.) Evaluating on the fundamental class,
"'$'"\\langle e(\\nu_\\alpha),[D_\\alpha]\\rangle=D_\\alpha\\cdot
D_\\alpha=0"'$, the self-intersection number. This is
Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction}.
\\end{proof}

\\begin{proof}[Proof of Corollary~\\ref{cor:cp2}]
Let "'$M='"\\CP"'^2$ with the Fubini--Study form $'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}}"'$
(normalised, say, so lines have positive area), and
$D=L'"\\cong\\CP"'^1$ a projective line: a smooth symplectic
hypersurface, i.e.'"\\ a symplectic SNC divisor with one component;
"'$'"\\CP"'^2$ is closed. The normal bundle of a line is
$'"\\nu_L=\\mathcal O_{\\CP"'^1}(1)$, so
$'"\\langle e(\\nu_L),[L]\\rangle=\\int_Lc_1(\\mathcal O(1))=1\\neq0"'$.
By Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction} no "'$'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}}"'$-tame
SNC-adapted $J$ exists.

Now allow the deformation: if $'"\\omega_1"'$ is another symplectic
form joined to $'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}}"'$ by a path $'"\\omega_t"'$ of
cohomologous symplectic forms along which $L$ remains a symplectic
SNC divisor, then Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction} applies equally to
"'$('"\\CP"'^2,'"\\omega_1,L)"'$ --- the self-intersection
$'"\\langle e(\\nu_L),[L]\\rangle=L\\cdot L=1"'$ is a topological
intersection number, unchanged by any symplectic deformation
keeping $L$ smooth and embedded --- so no $'"\\omega_1"'$-tame
SNC-adapted $J$ exists either. The same argument applies to two
distinct lines $L_1'"\\cup L_2"'$ (both components have
self-intersection $+1$), which is also a symplectic SNC divisor.
'"\\end{proof}

\\section{Remarks}\\label{sec:remarks}

\\noindent(1) The obstruction is genuinely about making the
\\emph{defining functions} holomorphic, not merely the strata. If
one only asks for an "'$'"\\omega"'$-tame $J$ under which the strata
$D_A$ are $J$-holomorphic ($J$-invariant tangent spaces), the
answer is easily '"\\emph{yes}: inside one Darboux SNC chart, take
the standard complex structure and extend arbitrarily; the point
of the present question is that the local defining functions
themselves must be holomorphic at every nearby point, and this
globalises into a local system that rigidifies the conormal
bundle.

\\noindent(2) The same proof gives: under the conclusion of the
question, the conormal complex line bundle of every compact
connected component has locally constant transition functions
relative to "'$J$-holomorphic defining frames (it is '"\\emph{flat}). The
vanishing of the Euler class is the resulting cohomological
shadow, sufficient for the counterexample.

\\noindent(3) For components with "'$D_'"\\alpha\\cdot D_\\alpha=0"'$ the
obstruction is silent; whether the property holds in that case (for
instance for a fibre in a product, where the conormal bundle is
trivial and the standard product complex structure works) is a
separate question. In the product
$X'"\\times\\Sigma"'$ with $D=X'"\\times\\{\\mathrm{pt}\\}"'$, an
$'"\\omega"'$-tame $J$ of the required kind '"\\emph{does} exist when "'$X$
carries a tame almost complex structure $J_X$ (take
$J_X'"\\oplus i"'$): the obstruction of Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction}
correctly gives "'$0$ there, since $'"\\nu_D"'$ is trivial.

'"\\noindent(4) The counterexample is robust: one may replace
"'$('"\\CP"'^2,L)$ by any closed symplectic $(M,'"\\omega)"'$ and any
symplectic SNC divisor having a component $D_'"\\alpha"'$ with
$'"\\langle e(\\nu_\\alpha),[D_\\alpha]\\rangle\\neq0"'$, e.g.'"\\ the
proper transform of a line inside a blow-up of "'$('"\\CP"'^2,
'"\\omega)"'$ (self-intersection $0$ or $-1$ accordingly, etc.'"\\ with
suitable normalisations), or an exceptional sphere with
self-intersection "'$-1$.

'"\\end{document}

\\title{No tame almost complex structure is adapted to a general\\\\
symplectic simple normal crossings divisor}
\\author{}
\\date{}
\\maketitle

\\begin{abstract}
\\noindent We show that the question has a negative answer. If
"'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ is a closed symplectic manifold, $D'"\\subset M"'$ a
symplectic simple normal crossings divisor, and $J$ an
$'"\\omega"'$-tame almost complex structure admitting local
$J$-holomorphic SNC coordinates near every point, then for every
component $D_'"\\alpha"'$ of $D$ the Euler class of the normal bundle of
$D_'"\\alpha"'$ vanishes in real cohomology, $'"\\langle
e(\\nu_{D_\\alpha}),[D_\\alpha]\\rangle=D_\\alpha\\cdot D_\\alpha=0"'$.
In particular, a projective line $L'"\\cong\\CP"'^1$ in
$('"\\CP"'^2,'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}})"'$ is a symplectic SNC divisor with
$L'"\\cdot L=1"'$, so no such $J$ exists for it; the allowed
cohomologous deformation of $'"\\omega"'$ cannot repair this. Hence the
answer to the question is '"\\emph{no} in general.
\\end{abstract}

\\section{The answer and the obstruction}\\label{sec:statement}

\\begin{quote}
\\textbf{Question.} Let "'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ be a closed symplectic manifold
and $D'"\\subset M"'$ a symplectic simple normal crossings divisor. Does
there exist an $'"\\omega"'$-tame almost complex structure $J$ such that
locally on $M$ there are smooth complex coordinates
$(z_1,'"\\ldots,z_n)"'$ in which, for some $0'"\\le r\\le n"'$, the functions
$z_1,'"\\ldots,z_r"'$ are $J$-holomorphic and $D$ is given by
$z_1'"\\cdots z_r=0"'$? (One may first deform $'"\\omega"'$ through
cohomologous symplectic forms keeping $D$ symplectic SNC.)
'"\\end{quote}

We call an almost complex structure "'$J$ with the local property
above '"\\emph{SNC-adapted to} "'$D$. Recall that $'"\\zeta"'$ is
'"\\emph{"'$J$-holomorphic} if
'"\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:CR}
\\dd\\zeta\\circ J\\ =\\ i\\,\\dd\\zeta
\\end{equation}
pointwise. Note the following immediate but crucial point: the
coordinates in the question are required only to exist on an open
neighbourhood of each point, but the condition~\\eqref{eq:CR} is
required \\emph{at every point of that neighbourhood}.

\\begin{theorem}[Obstruction]\\label{thm:obstruction}
Let "'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ be a symplectic manifold, $D'"\\subset M"'$ a symplectic
simple normal crossings divisor, and $J$ an $'"\\omega"'$-tame almost
complex structure SNC-adapted to $D$. Let $D_'"\\alpha"'$ be a
'"\\emph{compact connected} component of "'$D$. Then
'"\\[
\\langle e(\\nu_\\alpha),[D_\\alpha]\\rangle\\ =\\
D_\\alpha\\cdot D_\\alpha\\ =\\ 0,
\\]
where "'$'"\\nu_\\alpha"'$ is the normal bundle of $D_'"\\alpha"'$ (a complex
line bundle, oriented as in Section~'"\\ref{sec:obstruction}).
Equivalently, "'$e('"\\nu_\\alpha)=0"'$ in $H''^2(D_'"\\alpha;\\RR)"'$.
'"\\end{theorem}

\\begin{corollary}[Counterexample]\\label{cor:cp2}
Let "'$M='"\\CP"'^2$ with the Fubini--Study symplectic form
$'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}}"'$, and let $D=L'"\\cong\\CP"'^1$ be a projective
line. Then $D$ is a symplectic SNC divisor (a single smooth
component) in the closed symplectic manifold $('"\\CP"'^2,'"\\omega)"'$, and
$L'"\\cdot L=1\\neq0"'$; hence no $'"\\omega"'$-tame SNC-adapted $J$ exists.
Since the conclusion of Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction} is
topological ("'$L'"\\cdot L"'$ depends only on the homology class of $L$),
it is insensitive to any deformation $'"\\omega_t"'$ of
$'"\\omega=\\omega_0"'$ through cohomologous symplectic forms keeping $L$
symplectic, so the deformation allowed in the question cannot help.
The same conclusion holds with $D$ the union of two distinct lines
(a nodal SNC divisor), again because each component has
self-intersection $+1$.
'"\\end{corollary}

\\noindent\\emph{Answer to the question:} \\textbf{No}, not in
general: "'$('"\\CP"'^2,'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}},L)"'$ is an explicit
counterexample, and there is no path of cohomologous symplectic
forms after which $L$ admits an SNC-adapted tame almost complex
structure.

'"\\begin{remark}[Where the boundary lies]
The obstruction is sharp in the following sense: the proof uses
nothing but the existence of local "'$J$-holomorphic defining
functions whose zero set is the component, and the compactness of
the component. Components with $'"\\langle e(\\nu_\\alpha),
[D_\\alpha]\\rangle=0"'$ escape this particular obstruction.
'"\\end{remark}

\\section{Conventions and the first lemma}\\label{sec:first}

Throughout, "'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ is a symplectic manifold of dimension
$2n$, and $D='"\\bigcup_{\\alpha\\in I}D_\\alpha"'$ (finite union) is a
symplectic SNC divisor: every point $p$ has a Darboux chart whose
coordinates $(x_1,'"\\dots,x_n)"'$ satisfy $D'"\\cap U=\\{x_1\\cdots
x_r=0\\}"'$, with the components through $p$ equal to the
coordinate hyperplanes. Hence $D_'"\\alpha"'$ is a closed smooth
symplectic submanifold of codimension $2$, and for any subset
$A$ of indices, $D_A:='"\\bigcap_{\\alpha\\in A}D_\\alpha"'$ is a smooth
symplectic submanifold. Components are taken connected (replace a
disconnected component by its connected pieces).

'"\\begin{lemma}["'$J$ preserves all strata]'"\\label{lem:strata}
Let "'$J$ be SNC-adapted to $D$. Then for every point $p'"\\in D"'$ and
every index set $A$ with $p'"\\in D_A=\\bigcap_{\\alpha\\in A}D_\\alpha"'$,
the subspace $T_pD_A'"\\subset T_pM"'$ is $J_p$-invariant. Thus
$J_A:=J|_{TD_A}$ is an almost complex structure on $D_A$, and
$'"\\omega|_{D_A}"'$ tames $J_A$.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
At "'$p$, choose the adapted coordinates $(z_1,'"\\dots,z_n)"'$ given by
the SNC-adaptedness, with $D'"\\cap U=\\{z_1\\cdots z_r=0\\}"'$, the
components through $p$ being $'"\\{z_k=0\\}"'$, $k=1,'"\\dots,r"'$, and
$z_1,'"\\dots,z_r"'$ $J$-holomorphic on $U$. Then
$T_pD_A='"\\bigcap_{k:\\,\\alpha_k\\in A}\\ker \\dd z_k(p)"'$, where
$'"\\alpha_k"'$ is the component $'"\\{z_k=0\\}"'$. If $v'"\\in\\ker\\dd z_k(p)"'$,
then $'"\\dd z_k(Jv)=i\\,\\dd z_k(v)=0"'$, so $Jv'"\\in\\ker\\dd z_k(p)"'$.
Hence each $'"\\ker\\dd z_k(p)"'$ and their intersection is
$J_p$-invariant. Taming restricts: for $0'"\\neq v\\in T_pD_A"'$,
$'"\\omega(v,J_Av)=\\omega(v,Jv)>0"'$.
'"\\end{proof}

\\section{The maximum principle for "'$J$-holomorphic functions}
'"\\label{sec:max}

\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:max}
Let "'$(X,J)$ be a connected almost complex manifold without
boundary, and let $h'"\\colon X\\to\\CC"'$ be $J$-holomorphic
(Definition~'"\\eqref{eq:CR}). If "'$|h|$ attains a local maximum at a
point of $X$, then $h$ is constant. In particular, if $X$ is
compact then every $J$-holomorphic function $X'"\\to\\CC"'$ is constant.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
We use the standard local existence of pseudoholomorphic discs in
almost complex manifolds (Nijenhuis--Woolf): for every "'$p'"\\in X"'$ and
every complex line $'"\\ell\\subset T_pX"'$ ($J_p$-invariant real
$2$-plane), there is a $J$-holomorphic disc
$'"\\varphi\\colon(\\Delta,j)\\to(X,J)"'$ with $'"\\varphi(0)=p"'$ and
$'"\\varphi_*T_0\\Delta=\\ell"'$; moreover these discs depend smoothly on
parameters, so that the images of small discs centred at $p$
through all complex lines sweep out a full neighbourhood of $p$.

Suppose $|h|$ attains a local maximum at $p'"\\in X"'$, say $|h|'"\\le
|h(p)|"'$ near $p$. Let $'"\\varphi\\colon\\Delta\\to X"'$ be any small
$J$-holomorphic disc through $p$. Then $h'"\\circ\\varphi"'$ is a
holomorphic function $'"\\Delta\\to\\CC"'$ (chain rule from
'"\\eqref{eq:CR}), and "'$|h'"\\circ\\varphi|"'$ attains its maximum at
$0'"\\in\\Delta"'$; by the classical maximum modulus principle,
$h'"\\circ\\varphi"'$ is constant. In particular
$h'"\\equiv h(p)"'$ on $'"\\varphi(\\Delta)"'$. Varying the complex line
through $p$, the discs fill a neighbourhood $W$ of $p$ (by the
parameter statement above); hence $h'"\\equiv h(p)"'$ on $W$. So the set
$'"\\{h=h(p)\\}"'$ is open; it is also closed, and $X$ is connected, so
$h$ is constant everywhere. The compact case follows since $|h|$
attains a maximum.
'"\\end{proof}

\\begin{remark}\\label{rem:subharmonic}
Alternatively one can note that "'$|h|''^2$ is $J$-plurisubharmonic
(its restriction to every $J$-holomorphic disc is subharmonic),
and use the corresponding maximum principle; the disc argument
above is the direct route and needs nothing beyond
Nijenhuis--Woolf.
'"\\end{remark}

\\section{The cocycle of defining functions is constant}
\\label{sec:cocycle}

\\begin{proposition}\\label{prop:cocycle}
Let "'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$, $D$, $J$ be as in Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction},
and let "'$D_'"\\alpha"'$ be a compact connected component. Cover
$D_'"\\alpha"'$ by open sets $W_i'"\\subset M"'$ on which there are
$J$-holomorphic functions $'"\\zeta_i\\colon W_i\\to\\CC"'$ with
'"\\[
\\{q\\in W_i:\\zeta_i(q)=0\\}\\ =\\ D_\\alpha\\cap W_i,
\\qquad
\\dd\\zeta_i\\neq0\\ \\text{on }D_\\alpha\\cap W_i
\\tag{"'$'"\\ast"'$}
'"\\]
(such covers exist by SNC-adaptedness: take the first adapted
coordinate at each point of "'$D_'"\\alpha"'$). Then on each overlap
$W_i'"\\cap W_j"'$ the ratio $h_{ij}:='"\\zeta_i/\\zeta_j"'$, a priori
defined off $D_'"\\alpha"'$, extends to a smooth nonvanishing function
on $W_i'"\\cap W_j"'$ which is $J$-holomorphic; and its restriction to
$D_'"\\alpha"'$ is '"\\emph{constant} on each connected non-empty overlap
piece "'$W_i'"\\cap W_j\\cap D_\\alpha"'$.
'"\\end{proposition}

\\begin{proof}
\\emph{Step 1: the ratio and its extension.}
On "'$(W_i'"\\cap W_j)\\setminus D_\\alpha"'$ both $'"\\zeta_i,\\zeta_j"'$ are
nonzero (their zero sets in $W_i,W_j$ are exactly the $D_'"\\alpha"'$
part, by ($'"\\ast"'$)), so $h_{ij}='"\\zeta_i/\\zeta_j"'$ is smooth,
nonvanishing, and $J$-holomorphic there (a quotient of
$J$-holomorphic functions is $J$-holomorphic: one checks
'"\\eqref{eq:CR} by Leibniz' rule). Both "'$'"\\zeta_i"'$ and $'"\\zeta_j"'$
vanish exactly on $D_'"\\alpha\\cap W_i\\cap W_j"'$ with $'"\\dd\\zeta\\neq0"'$
along it, so in a tubular neighbourhood of this codimension-2
submanifold both have a simple zero in the normal direction; their
quotient therefore extends smoothly and nonvanishingly across
$D_'"\\alpha"'$, still satisfying $h_{ij}'"\\zeta_j=\\zeta_i"'$.
Differentiating this identity at $q'"\\in D_\\alpha"'$ gives
$'"\\dd\\zeta_i(q)=h_{ij}(q)\\,\\dd\\zeta_j(q)"'$ (the term
$'"\\zeta_j\\,\\dd h_{ij}"'$ vanishes since $'"\\zeta_j(q)=0"'$), so
$h_{ij}(q)'"\\neq0"'$ at the extension as well.

'"\\emph{Step 2: "'$J$-holomorphicity across $D_'"\\alpha"'$.}
The identity $'"\\dd h_{ij}\\circ J=i\\,\\dd h_{ij}"'$ holds on the dense
open set where $h_{ij}$ was first defined; all quantities are
smooth up to and across $D_'"\\alpha"'$ by Step 1, so the identity
persists on the whole of $W_i'"\\cap W_j"'$ by continuity. In
particular, restricting to the $J$-invariant subbundle $TD_'"\\alpha"'$
(Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:strata}), the function
"'$h_'"\\alpha:=h_{ij}|_{D_\\alpha\\cap W_i\\cap W_j}"'$ is
$J_'"\\alpha"'$-holomorphic, where $J_'"\\alpha=J|_{TD_\\alpha}"'$.

'"\\emph{Step 3: constancy on the divisor.}
"'$D_'"\\alpha"'$ is compact and connected; $|h_'"\\alpha|"'$ attains its
maximum, and $h_'"\\alpha"'$ is $J_'"\\alpha"'$-holomorphic, so
Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:max} gives "'$|h_'"\\alpha|"'$ constant... in fact the
lemma gives that $h_'"\\alpha"'$ is constant directly. Apply
Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:max} to
"'$h_'"\\alpha\\colon(D_\\alpha,J_\\alpha)\\to\\CC"'$: it is a
$J_'"\\alpha"'$-holomorphic function on a compact connected almost
complex manifold, hence constant (where the value is nonzero, as
$h_{ij}'"\\neq0"'$). This proves the proposition on each connected
overlap piece.
'"\\end{proof}

\\section{Euler classes and the obstruction}\\label{sec:obstruction}

\\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\\ref{thm:obstruction}]
Let "'$D_'"\\alpha"'$ be a compact connected component. The normal bundle
'"\\[
\\nu_\\alpha\\ :=\\ TM|_{D_\\alpha}/TD_\\alpha
\\]
is a real vector bundle of rank "'$2$; since $TD_'"\\alpha"'$ is
$J$-invariant (Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:strata}), "'$J$ descends to a fibrewise
complex structure on $'"\\nu_\\alpha"'$, making it a complex line bundle,
and we orient $'"\\nu_\\alpha"'$ as a complex line bundle (this is the
usual orientation for the self-intersection of a divisor). The
conormal bundle $'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$ is the dual complex line bundle.

Choose a cover $'"\\{W_i\\}"'$ of $D_'"\\alpha"'$ and $J$-holomorphic defining
functions $'"\\zeta_i"'$ as in Proposition~'"\\ref{prop:cocycle}. On
"'$D_'"\\alpha\\cap W_i"'$ the linear form
$e_i:='"\\dd\\zeta_i|_{D_\\alpha}"'$ annihilates $TD_'"\\alpha"'$ (as
$'"\\zeta_i|_{D_\\alpha}=0"'$), hence descends to a section of the
'"\\emph{complexified} conormal bundle, and by ("'$'"\\ast"'$) it is
nowhere zero: $e_i$ is a local frame of
$'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*'"\\otimes\\CC"'$. In fact $e_i$ is $'"\\CC"'$-linear with
respect to $J$: for $v'"\\in T_qM"'$, $q'"\\in D_\\alpha"'$,
$e_i(Jv)='"\\dd\\zeta_i(Jv)=i\\dd\\zeta_i(v)=i\\,e_i(v)"'$, so $e_i$ is a
$'"\\CC"'$-linear functional
$'"\\nu_\\alpha\\to\\CC"'$, i.e.'"\\ a nowhere zero section of the complex
line bundle "'$'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$ (with its $J$ complex structure). On
overlaps,
'"\\[
e_i\\ =\\ h_{ij}\\,e_j
\\qquad\\text{with }h_{ij}\\neq0\\ \\emph{constant on every connected
overlap piece}
\\]
by Proposition~\\ref{prop:cocycle}. Hence "'$'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$ admits a
trivialising cover with '"\\emph{constant} transition functions
"'$C''^'"\\times"'$-valued, i.e.'"\\ "'$'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$ is a flat complex line
bundle: the constant transition functions $'"\\{h_{ij}\\}"'$ have zero
derivatives, so any local flat connections patch to a global flat
connection on $'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$.

A flat line bundle has vanishing real first Chern class (take the
curvature of the flat connection: it vanishes identically, so by
Chern--Weil theory $c_1=0$ in $H''^2(D_'"\\alpha;\\RR)"'$). Therefore
'"\\[
e(\\nu_\\alpha)\\ =\\ -\\,c_1(\\nu_\\alpha"'^*)'"\\ =\\ 0
\\ \\in\\ H"'^2(D_'"\\alpha;\\RR).
\\]
(For a complex line bundle, the Euler class of the underlying
oriented real plane bundle equals the first Chern class, and duals
change the sign.) Evaluating on the fundamental class,
"'$'"\\langle e(\\nu_\\alpha),[D_\\alpha]\\rangle=D_\\alpha\\cdot
D_\\alpha=0"'$, the self-intersection number. This is
Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction}.
\\end{proof}

\\begin{proof}[Proof of Corollary~\\ref{cor:cp2}]
Let "'$M='"\\CP"'^2$ with the Fubini--Study form $'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}}"'$
(normalised, say, so lines have positive area), and
$D=L'"\\cong\\CP"'^1$ a projective line: a smooth symplectic
hypersurface, i.e.'"\\ a symplectic SNC divisor with one component;
"'$'"\\CP"'^2$ is closed. The normal bundle of a line is
$'"\\nu_L=\\mathcal O_{\\CP"'^1}(1)$, so
$'"\\langle e(\\nu_L),[L]\\rangle=\\int_Lc_1(\\mathcal O(1))=1\\neq0"'$.
By Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction} no "'$'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}}"'$-tame
SNC-adapted $J$ exists.

Now allow the deformation: if $'"\\omega_1"'$ is another symplectic
form joined to $'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}}"'$ by a path $'"\\omega_t"'$ of
cohomologous symplectic forms along which $L$ remains a symplectic
SNC divisor, then Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction} applies equally to
"'$('"\\CP"'^2,'"\\omega_1,L)"'$ --- the self-intersection
$'"\\langle e(\\nu_L),[L]\\rangle=L\\cdot L=1"'$ is a topological
intersection number, unchanged by any symplectic deformation
keeping $L$ smooth and embedded --- so no $'"\\omega_1"'$-tame
SNC-adapted $J$ exists either. The same argument applies to two
distinct lines $L_1'"\\cup L_2"'$ (both components have
self-intersection $+1$), which is also a symplectic SNC divisor.
'"\\end{proof}

\\section{Remarks}\\label{sec:remarks}

\\noindent(1) The obstruction is genuinely about making the
\\emph{defining functions} holomorphic, not merely the strata. If
one only asks for an "'$'"\\omega"'$-tame $J$ under which the strata
$D_A$ are $J$-holomorphic ($J$-invariant tangent spaces), the
answer is easily '"\\emph{yes}: inside one Darboux SNC chart, take
the standard complex structure and extend arbitrarily; the point
of the present question is that the local defining functions
themselves must be holomorphic at every nearby point, and this
globalises into a local system that rigidifies the conormal
bundle.

\\noindent(2) The same proof gives: under the conclusion of the
question, the conormal complex line bundle of every compact
connected component has locally constant transition functions
relative to "'$J$-holomorphic defining frames (it is '"\\emph{flat}). The
vanishing of the Euler class is the resulting cohomological
shadow, sufficient for the counterexample.

\\noindent(3) For components with "'$D_'"\\alpha\\cdot D_\\alpha=0"'$ the
obstruction is silent; whether the property holds in that case (for
instance for a fibre in a product, where the conormal bundle is
trivial and the standard product complex structure works) is a
separate question. In the product
$X'"\\times\\Sigma"'$ with $D=X'"\\times\\{\\mathrm{pt}\\}"'$, an
$'"\\omega"'$-tame $J$ of the required kind '"\\emph{does} exist when "'$X$
carries a tame almost complex structure $J_X$ (take
$J_X'"\\oplus i"'$): the obstruction of Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction}
correctly gives "'$0$ there, since $'"\\nu_D"'$ is trivial.

'"\\noindent(4) The counterexample is robust: one may replace
"'$('"\\CP"'^2,L)$ by any closed symplectic $(M,'"\\omega)"'$ and any
symplectic SNC divisor having a component $D_'"\\alpha"'$ with
$'"\\langle e(\\nu_\\alpha),[D_\\alpha]\\rangle\\neq0"'$, e.g.'"\\ the
proper transform of a line inside a blow-up of "'$('"\\CP"'^2,
'"\\omega)"'$ (self-intersection $0$ or $-1$ accordingly, etc.'"\\ with
suitable normalisations), or an exceptional sphere with
self-intersection "'$-1$.

'"\\end{document}

\\begin{document}

\\title{Tame almost complex structures adapted to symplectic\\\\
simple normal crossings divisors}
\\author{}
\\date{}
\\maketitle

\\begin{abstract}
\\noindent Let "'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ be a closed symplectic manifold and
$D'"\\subset M"'$ a symplectic simple normal crossings divisor. We prove
that there exists an $'"\\omega"'$-tame almost complex structure $J$ such
that every point of $M$ has a neighbourhood with smooth complex
coordinates $(z_1,'"\\dots,z_n)"'$ in which, for some $0'"\\le r\\le n"'$, the
functions $z_1,'"\\dots,z_r"'$ are $J$-holomorphic and $D$ is given by
$z_1'"\\cdots z_r=0"'$. No deformation of $'"\\omega"'$ is needed: the constant
path $'"\\omega_t=\\omega"'$ works.
'"\\end{abstract}

\\section{Statement and strategy}\\label{sec:statement}

\\begin{theorem}[Main theorem]\\label{thm:main}
Let "'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ be a closed symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$ and
let $D'"\\subset M"'$ be a symplectic simple normal crossings divisor. Then
there exists a smooth $'"\\omega"'$-tame almost complex structure $J$ on
$M$ such that every point $p$ of $M$ has a neighbourhood $U$ with
smooth complex coordinates
$(z_1,'"\\dots,z_n)\\colon U\\to U'\\subset\\CC"'^n$ satisfying:
'"\\begin{enumerate}
\\item[\\normalfont(i)] "'$D'"\\cap U=\\{q\\in U:z_1(q)\\cdots z_r(q)=0\\}"'$ for
some $0'"\\le r\\le n"'$;

\\langle e(\\nu_\\alpha),[D_\\alpha]\\rangle

\\begin{corollary}[The counterexample]\\label{cor:cp2}

single component trivially constitutes simple normal crossings. But
'"\\[
L\\cdot L\\ =\\ \\int_L c_1\\bigl(\\mathcal O_{\\CP"'^1}(1)'"\\bigr)\\ =\\ 1
\\ \\neq\\ 0 ,
\\]

Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction}, no "'$'"\\omega'"'$-tame SNC-adapted $J$

'"\\end{remark}

\\section{Strata are "'$J$-invariant}'"\\label{sec:strata}

\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:strata}
Let "'$J$ be SNC-adapted to $D$ (no taming assumption needed). Then
for every $p'"\\in D"'$, and $A:='"\\{\\alpha:p\\in D_\\alpha\\}"'$, the tangent
space $T_pD_A$ of the stratum $D_A='"\\bigcap_{\\alpha\\in A}D_\\alpha"'$
is a $J_p$-complex subspace of $T_pM$. Consequently
$J_A:=J|_{TD_A}$ is an almost complex structure on $D_A$, and, if
$J$ is $'"\\omega"'$-tame, so is $J_A$ (with respect to
$'"\\omega|_{D_A}"'$).

\\begin{proof}
Choose adapted coordinates "'$(z_1,'"\\dots,z_n)"'$ at $p$ with
$D'"\\cap U=\\{z_1\\cdots z_r=0\\}"'$, so that $D_A'"\\cap U=\\{z_{k}=
0:\\alpha_k\\in A\\}"'$ after numbering, and
$T_pD_A='"\\bigcap_{k:\\,\\alpha_k\\in A}\\ker\\dd z_k(p)"'$. For
$v'"\\in\\ker\\dd z_k(p)"'$, the $J$-holomorphicity of $z_k$ gives
$'"\\dd z_k(Jv)=i\\,\\dd z_k(v)=0"'$, so $Jv'"\\in\\ker\\dd z_k(p)"'$. Thus each

\\begin{corollary}[Normal bundle is a complex line bundle]
\\label{cor:normal}
For any component "'$D_'"\\alpha"'$, the normal bundle
$'"\\nu_\\alpha:=TM|_{D_\\alpha}/TD_\\alpha"'$ carries a fibrewise complex
structure induced by $J$, making it a complex line bundle over
$D_'"\\alpha"'$; the conormal bundle $'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*='"\\Hom_\\CC(\\nu_\\alpha,

'"\\end{corollary}

\\section{The ratio lemma}\\label{sec:ratio}

\\begin{lemma}[Ratios are "'$J$-holomorphic across the divisor]
'"\\label{lem:ratio}
Let "'$J$ be SNC-adapted, and let $'"\\zeta,\\zeta'"'$ be $J$-holomorphic
functions on a connected open set $W'"\\subset M"'$ with
'"\\[
\\{\\zeta=0\\}\\ =\\ \\{\\zeta'=0\\}\\ =\\ W\\cap D_\\alpha,
\\qquad \\dd\\zeta\\neq0,\\ \\dd\\zeta'\\neq0\\ \\text{on }W\\cap D_\\alpha .
\\]
Then the ratio "'$h:='"\\zeta'/\\zeta"'$, smooth and nonvanishing on
$W'"\\setminus D_\\alpha"'$, extends to a smooth nonvanishing function on
$W$, the extension satisfies
'"\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:cross}
\\dd\\zeta'\\ =\\ h\\,\\dd\\zeta\\quad\\text{on }W\\cap D_\\alpha,
\\end{equation}
and "'$h$ is $J$-holomorphic on $W$: $'"\\dd h\\circ J=i\\,\\dd h"'$.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
Off "'$D_'"\\alpha"'$, both functions are nowhere zero, so $h$ is smooth
nonvanishing there, and the computation
$'"\\dd\\zeta'=\\dd h\\,\\zeta+h\\,\\dd\\zeta"'$ composed with $J$ gives, using
$'"\\dd\\zeta\\circ J=i\\dd\\zeta"'$ and $'"\\dd\\zeta'\\circ J=i\\dd\\zeta'"'$,
'"\\[
0\\ =\\ \\zeta\\cdot\\bigl(\\dd h\\circ J-i\\,\\dd h\\bigr),
\\]
hence "'$'"\\dd h\\circ J=i\\dd h"'$ on $W'"\\setminus D_\\alpha"'$: $h$ is
$J$-holomorphic there.

For the extension: $D_'"\\alpha\\cap W"'$ is a smooth codimension-two
submanifold along which both $'"\\zeta,\\zeta'"'$ vanish with nonvanishing
differential transversely. In any tubular neighbourhood with normal
coordinate, both ${'"\\zeta}"'$ and ${'"\\zeta}'"'$ have a simple zero along
the zero section; their quotient extends smoothly and nonvanishingly
across the zero section (one-variable Taylor argument in the normal
direction: if $f(t)=t'"\\,F(t)"'$, $g(t)=t'"\\,G(t)"'$ with $F(0),G(0)'"\\neq0"'$,
then $f/g=F/G$ extends). Differentiating
$'"\\zeta'=h\\zeta"'$ at $q'"\\in D_\\alpha"'$ (where $'"\\zeta=0"'$) yields
'"\\eqref{eq:cross}, and since "'$'"\\dd\\zeta'(q)\\neq0"'$ and
$'"\\dd\\zeta(q)\\neq0"'$, the extended $h$ is nonvanishing also on
$D_'"\\alpha"'$.

Finally, the identity $'"\\dd h\\circ J=i\\dd h"'$ holds on
$W'"\\setminus D_\\alpha"'$, both sides are continuous on $W$ (since $h$
and $J$ are smooth on $W$), and $W'"\\setminus D_\\alpha"'$ is dense in
$W$; hence the identity holds on all of $W$.
'"\\end{proof}

\\section{The maximum principle}\\label{sec:max}

\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:max}
Let "'$(X,J)$ be a connected almost complex manifold of dimension
$2m'"\\ge2"'$, and $h'"\\colon X\\to\\CC"'$ $J$-holomorphic. If $|h|$ has a
local maximum at some point of $X$, then $h$ is constant. In
particular, on a compact connected almost complex manifold every
$J$-holomorphic function is constant.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
We use the local existence of "'$J$-holomorphic discs in almost
complex manifolds (Nijenhuis--Woolf): for every $p'"\\in X"'$ and every
complex line $'"\\ell\\subset(T_pX,J_p)"'$ there is a $J$-holomorphic disc
$'"\\varphi\\colon\\Delta\\to X"'$ with $'"\\varphi(0)=p"'$ and
$'"\\varphi_{*}T_0\\Delta=\\ell"'$; moreover one can choose such discs
smoothly depending on parameters (e.g.'"\\ on the line and on nearby
points), so that their images through "'$'"\\{p'\\}\\times\\{"'$lines in
$T_{p'"'}X\\}"'$ cover a neighbourhood of $p$.

Suppose $|h|$ attains a local maximum at $p$. For any small
$J$-holomorphic disc $'"\\varphi\\colon\\Delta\\to X"'$ with
$'"\\varphi(0)=p"'$, the composition $h'"\\circ\\varphi"'$ is holomorphic
$'"\\Delta\\to\\CC"'$ (chain rule from $'"\\dd h\\circ J=i\\dd h"'$), and
$|h'"\\circ\\varphi|"'$ attains a maximum at $0$; by the classical
maximum modulus principle $h'"\\circ\\varphi"'$ is constant, in
particular $h|_{'"\\varphi(\\Delta)}\\equiv h(p)"'$. Since such discs
through $p$ sweep a neighbourhood of $p$ (choose the disc family as
above), $h'"\\equiv h(p)"'$ on an open set containing $p$. Thus
$'"\\{q:h(q)=h(p)\\}"'$ is open; it is also closed, and $X$ is
connected, so $h'"\\equiv h(p)"'$. The compact case follows because
$|h|$ attains its maximum.
'"\\end{proof}

\\section{Proof of the obstruction}\\label{sec:proof}

\\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\\ref{thm:obstruction}]
Let "'$D_'"\\alpha"'$ be a compact connected component; all components are
smooth codimension-$2$ symplectic submanifolds, and we use the
conormal complex line bundle $'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$ of
Corollary~'"\\ref{cor:normal}.

\\emph{Step 1: "'$J$-holomorphic conormal frames.}
By SNC-adaptedness, cover $D_'"\\alpha"'$ by finitely many adapted
coordinate neighbourhoods $W_i$, with adapted coordinates
$(z_1''^{(i)},'"\\dots,z_n"'^{(i)})$ in which $z_1''^{(i)}$ is
$J$-holomorphic and $'"\\{z_1"'^{(i)}=0'"\\}=D_\\alpha\\cap W_i"'$: indeed, at
any $p'"\\in D_\\alpha"'$, among the components through $p$ one is
$D_'"\\alpha"'$, and renumbering the adapted coordinates puts it first
(if $p'"\\notin D_\\alpha\\setminus\\bigcup_{\\beta\\neq\\alpha}D_\\beta"'$
there is nothing to check near $p$ for the frames below: points of
$D_'"\\alpha"'$ on other components are fine: adapted coordinates exist
there too, with $D_'"\\alpha"'$ as one of the coordinate hyperplanes).
On $W_i'"\\cap D_\\alpha"'$, set
'"\\[
e_i\\ :=\\ \\dd z_1"'^{(i)}'"\\big|_{D_\\alpha\\cap W_i}
\\ \\in\\ \\Gamma\\bigl(D_\\alpha\\cap W_i,\\ T"'^*M'"\\otimes\\CC\\bigr).
\\]
Since "'$z_1''^{(i)}|_{D_'"\\alpha\\cap W_i}=0"'$, $e_i$ annihilates
$T(D_'"\\alpha)"'$, so it descends to a homomorphism
$'"\\nu_\\alpha\\to\\CC"'$; since $'"\\dd z_1"'^{(i)}'"\\neq0"'$ along $D_'"\\alpha"'$
(it is a coordinate differential), $e_i'"\\neq0"'$ everywhere on
$D_'"\\alpha\\cap W_i"'$; and by $J$-holomorphicity,
$e_i(Jv)='"\\dd z_1"'^{(i)}(Jv)=i'"\\,\\dd z_1"'^{(i)}(v)=i'"\\,e_i(v)"'$, so $e_i$
is $'"\\CC"'$-linear for the complex structure of
Corollary~'"\\ref{cor:normal}: "'$e_i$ is a nowhere vanishing local frame
of the complex line bundle $'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$.

'"\\emph{Step 2: constant transition functions.}
On "'$W_i'"\\cap W_j"'$, both $z_1''^{(i)}$ and $z_1''^{(j)}$ are
$J$-holomorphic defining functions of
$D_'"\\alpha\\cap W_i\\cap W_j"'$, with the hypotheses of
Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:ratio}. Hence the ratio
"'$h_{ij}:=z_1''^{(j)}/z_1''^{(i)}$ extends smoothly and nonvanishingly
across $D_'"\\alpha"'$, is $J$-holomorphic on $W_i'"\\cap W_j"'$, and
$e_j=h_{ij}'"\\,e_i"'$ on $D_'"\\alpha\\cap W_i\\cap W_j"'$ (this is
'"\\eqref{eq:cross}). Restricting to "'$D_'"\\alpha"'$: by
Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:strata}, "'$J_'"\\alpha:=J|_{TD_\\alpha}"'$ is an almost
complex structure on the compact connected manifold $D_'"\\alpha"'$, and
$h_{ij}|_{D_'"\\alpha}"'$ is $J_'"\\alpha"'$-holomorphic: indeed
$'"\\dd(h_{ij}|_{D_\\alpha})\\circ J_\\alpha=(\\dd h_{ij}\\circ J)|_{TD_\\alpha}
=i\\,\\dd h_{ij}|_{TD_\\alpha}=i\\,\\dd(h_{ij}|_{D_\\alpha})"'$. By
Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:max}, "'$h_{ij}|_{D_'"\\alpha}"'$ is constant on every
connected component of $D_'"\\alpha\\cap W_i\\cap W_j"'$.

'"\\emph{Step 3: flatness and vanishing Euler class.}
The complex line bundle "'$'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$ thus admits a trivialising
cover (the $e_i$) whose transition functions
$'"\\{h_{ij}|_{D_\\alpha}\\}"'$ are constant on each connected overlap
piece. Choose on each $W_i'"\\cap D_\\alpha"'$ the connection whose
covariant derivative kills $e_i$; since on overlaps the frames
differ by constants, these local connections agree on overlaps and
assemble to a global connection $'"\\nabla"'$ on $'"\\nu_\\alpha"'^*$ with
$'"\\nabla e_i=0"'$ on $W_i$; its curvature satisfies
$'"\\Omega(e_i)=0"'$ locally, hence $'"\\Omega\\equiv0"'$: $'"\\nabla"'$ is flat.
By Chern--Weil theory (the first Chern form of a flat
connection is identically zero),
'"\\[
c_1(\\nu_\\alpha"'^*)'"\\ =\\ 0\\ \\in\\ H"'^2(D_'"\\alpha;\\RR).
\\]
For a complex line bundle, the Euler class of the oriented real
plane bundle equals "'$c_1$, and duals reverse the sign; hence
'"\\[
e(\\nu_\\alpha)\\ =\\ c_1(\\nu_\\alpha)\\ =\\ -c_1(\\nu_\\alpha"'^*)'"\\ =\\ 0 ,
\\qquad
\\langle e(\\nu_\\alpha),[D_\\alpha]\\rangle=0 .
\\]
The self-intersection "'$D_'"\\alpha\\cdot D_\\alpha:=\\langle
e(\\nu_\\alpha),[D_\\alpha]\\rangle"'$ therefore vanishes.
'"\\end{proof}

\\begin{proof}[Proof of Corollary~\\ref{cor:cp2}]
"'$('"\\CP"'^2,'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}})"'$ is a closed symplectic manifold and
a projective line $L$ is a smooth symplectic hypersurface; SNC for a
single component is automatic. Its normal bundle is
$'"\\mathcal O(1)"'$ with $c_1$ evaluating to $1$ on $[L]$; so the
conclusion of Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction} fails: no
"'$'"\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}}"'$-tame SNC-adapted $J$ exists.

For the deformation clause: suppose $'"\\{\\omega_t\\}_{t\\in[0,1]}"'$ is a
path of cohomologous symplectic forms with $'"\\omega_0=
\\omega_{\\mathrm{FS}}"'$, along which $L$ remains a symplectic SNC
divisor. Apply Theorem~'"\\ref{thm:obstruction} to
"'$('"\\CP"'^2,'"\\omega_1,L)"'$: the hypothesis "$J$ is $'"\\omega_1"'$-tame and
SNC-adapted" implies $L'"\\cdot L=0"'$; but $L'"\\cdot L"'$ is the
topological intersection number of the homology class

exists after any allowed deformation either. For
$D=L_1'"\\cup L_2"'$: at intersection points, linear coordinates provide
the SNC model (both are smooth symplectic hypersurfaces meeting
transversely --- but symplectic '"\\emph{orthogonality} is not required
in the question's notion; the SNC-Darboux model exists for any two
transverse symplectic hypersurfaces by the symplectic SNC
neighbourhood theorem: this is the standard definition; in any case
the obstruction statement only used adaptedness); each
component has "'$L_i'"\\cdot L_i=1"'$, so the same conclusion holds.
'"\\end{proof}

\\section{Discussion of sharpness}\\label{sec:remarks}

\\noindent(1) \\emph{What the obstruction uses.} Only the existence of
local "'$J$-holomorphic defining functions and the compactness of the
component enter: the ratio lemma makes the conormal frames constant
along the component via the maximum principle. Tameness of $J$,
closedness of $M$, and the SNC condition beyond smoothness of the
component are superfluous for the obstruction --- but $('"\\CP"'^2,L)$
satisfies all the hypotheses of the question, so the answer to the
question as stated is no.

'"\\noindent(2) \\emph{The deformation does not help because the
obstruction is not symplectic.} Theorem~\\ref{thm:obstruction} is a
statement about "'$J$ and $D$ alone (given adaptedness); its
conclusion $D_'"\\alpha\\cdot D_\\alpha=0"'$ is a topological fact of the
pair. No change of $'"\\omega"'$ within its cohomology class (or any
class) affects it, as long as $D_'"\\alpha"'$ stays compact.

'"\\noindent(3) \\emph{Sharpness of the principle.} The obstruction
vanishes when "'$D_'"\\alpha\\cdot D_\\alpha=0"'$; in product situations
(e.g.'"\\ "'$D=X'"\\times\\{0\\}\\subset X\\times\\Sigma"'^g$ with product form,
where $'"\\nu_D"'$ is trivial) adapted tame structures do exist
($J_X'"\\oplus"'$ standard), so no obstruction-free statement can
distinguish those cases with the invariant used here; whether the
answer is yes whenever all components have vanishing normal Euler
class is a further question not decided here.

'"\\noindent(4) \\emph{More counterexamples.} Any closed symplectic
"'$(M,'"\\omega)"'$ containing a symplectic SNC divisor with a compact
connected component $D_'"\\alpha"'$ of nonzero self-intersection is a
counterexample: a line in $'"\\CP"'^2$ (self-intersection $+1$), an
exceptional sphere in a symplectic blow-up (self-intersection $-1$),
a smooth fibre... note the fibre of a ruled surface has
self-intersection $0$, which does not obstruct; the anti-canonical
divisor in toric Fano symplectic manifolds has components with
nonzero pairing in many cases. In each case the answer to the
question is negative, stably under the allowed deformation.

possesses a flat connection; in particular its Euler class satisfies
\\[
e(\\nu_\\alpha)\\ =\\ 0\\ \\in\\ H"'^2(D_'"\\alpha;\\RR),

$J$-holomorphic defining functions of

Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:ratio}. Hence the ratio
"'$h_{ij}:=z_1''^{(j)}/z_1''^{(i)}$ extends smoothly and nonvanishingly

Scope: mathematical problem-solving / adapted-structure existence questions
